fix(ci): run the release-script unit tests
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into issue-150-d2a86da93c14

fix(ci): run the release-script unit tests

`scripts/*.rs` carries 78 `#[test]` functions across nine rust-scripts and
no workflow ran a single one of them. `cargo test` only builds the library
crate, so the release-script regression guards -- including the
rebase-before-stage ordering check in `version-and-commit.rs`, which exists
because a release once died with "cannot rebase: Your index contains
uncommitted changes" -- had never executed in CI.

Two suites had rotted unnoticed as a direct consequence:

* `create-github-release.rs` did not compile in test mode. It declared its
  `release_naming` module only under `#[cfg(not(test))]` and substituted a
  `super::` path that resolves to nothing when `rust-script --test` builds
  the file as its own crate root. Declared unconditionally instead.
* `version-and-commit.rs` and `wait-for-crate.rs` failed under the
  workflow-level `RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings`: a test harness has no `main`, so
  every helper reachable only from `main` is reported unused. Relaxed for
  test builds only, via `#![cfg_attr(test, allow(dead_code, ...))]`; the
  real script build still denies both.

`scripts/test-scripts.sh` runs every suite under the same `-Dwarnings` and
reports all failing scripts rather than stopping at the first, so it serves
as both the CI step and the documented local command. The new
`script-tests` job runs it, `build` is gated on it so a broken release
script cannot reach `auto-release`, and `pipeline-status` observes it.

`tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_150.rs` pins the fixes and the wiring. Verified: the
runner exits 1 on the pre-fix scripts and 0 after, with 78 tests passing.

Fixes #150

fix(ci): scope crates.io credentials to the publish steps

fix(ci): scope crates.io credentials to the publish steps

The workflow-level env: in release.yml declared CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN and
CARGO_TOKEN, and a workflow-level env is inherited by every job — including
the pull_request jobs that compile and run code from the branch under review
(build.rs, procedural macros, the tests themselves). Any branch pull request
could read the publish token out of its own environment.

Both publishing steps already declare the credentials at step level, so the
workflow-level declaration bought nothing. Remove it, and pin the invariant
with tests asserting that no workflow-level env value anywhere under
.github/workflows references secrets. and that both publish steps still
declare the tokens.

Fixes #149

ci: audit workflows with zizmor and fix the defects it reports

ci: audit workflows with zizmor and fix the defects it reports

workflows.yml ran actionlint only, so workflow security defects that
actionlint cannot see shipped with the template: dtolnay/rust-toolchain
pinned to the mutable `stable` branch in ten release jobs holding
`contents: write`, checkouts persisting GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config, and
contexts interpolated straight into `run:` blocks.

Add the zizmor job and .github/zizmor.yml (blanket hash-pin policy,
ref-pin for trusted first-party namespaces), hash-pin every third-party
action, set persist-credentials: false on all read-only checkouts, and
move context expansions into env:. Both actionlint 1.7.7 and zizmor
1.30.0 now report zero findings.

Closes #147

Merge pull request #144 from link-foundation/issue-143-3916e3712307

fix(release): stop reporting a throttled crates.io probe as a failed release

fix(release): stop reporting a throttled crates.io probe as a failed release

`scripts/wait-for-crate.rs` returned a bare `bool`, so a 403, 429 or 5xx from
crates.io was indistinguishable from "this version is not published yet". The
wait exhausted every attempt and failed the workflow with `<crate>@<version>
was not visible on crates.io`, pointing the reader at a publish step that had
actually succeeded.

The probe now returns a `Visibility` (`Published` / `NotPublishedYet` /
`Unknown`). When no attempt ever got a definitive answer, the error says the
release status could not be determined and shows how to check the sparse index,
instead of claiming the release did not happen.

Also in the same area:
- probe the sparse index (https://index.crates.io), which is what `cargo`
  resolves against and is not rate limited, with the JSON API as fallback
- put contact information in the User-Agent, as crates.io asks

Fixes #143

fix(ci): match code-change exclusions relative to the Rust package root

fix(ci): match code-change exclusions relative to the Rust package root

git diff --name-only prints repository-root-relative paths, while the
exclusion list of detect-code-changes.rs is expressed relative to the Rust
package root. In the multi-language layout (rust/Cargo.toml) that rust-paths.rs
supports, no excluded folder ever matched, so an examples/- or changelog.d/-only
pull request was reported as any-code-changed=true.

Strip the detected package prefix before matching, and treat files of other
languages (python/pyproject.toml, ...) as out of scope while keeping shared
paths (.github/, scripts/, repository-root files) in scope.

Fixes #139

Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into issue-135-89e38c7f374e

ci: give long steps an execution budget that expires before timeout-minutes

GitHub reports a job killed by `timeout-minutes` as `cancelled`, not `failed`.
On a non-default ref that is indistinguishable from a run superseded by
`cancel-in-progress`, so `check-pipeline-status.sh` only escalated it to an
error on `main` and a genuine timeout on a pull request produced no failure
anywhere.

`timeout-minutes` is a backstop, never the deadline. Whenever unbudgeted setup
time plus a step's own runtime can exceed the job cap, the runner wins the race
and the failure mode silently degrades from `failure` to `cancelled`.

- Add `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh`. It uses `set -m` so the command gets
  its own process group -- `timeout(1)` and a plain `kill $pid` reach only the
  direct child, while `cargo test` spawns a tree whose orphans keep the runner
  busy. It SIGTERMs the group, waits a grace period, SIGKILLs, and exits 124
  with a `::error` annotation naming the budget and the overrun, plus a
  `::warning` at 70% while it can still be acted on.
- Budget the long steps in `release.yml` (`test`, `coverage`, `fresh-merge`).
  The test job's cap moves 20 -> 30 minutes so its budgets fit under the share
  ceiling. `docker-build` builds through a `uses:` action with no shell command
  to wrap and is an explicit exemption.
- Add `tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_135.rs`, making "the budget expires before the
  cap" a checked invariant rather than a per-job accident: every job declares
  `timeout-minutes`, and each job's budgets sum to at most 70% of its cap. This
  is what finds the next instance.
- Point the non-default-ref warning in `check-pipeline-status.sh` at the
  `has exceeded the maximum execution time` annotation.

Fixes #135

Issue: https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/135

fix(links): report non-HTTP lychee errors instead of claiming all archived

extractBrokenUrls() only matched http(s) links, so lychee errors with no
URL to look up in the Wayback Machine (missing local files, unresolvable
root-relative links) were dropped. When they were the only errors the
script printed 'No broken URLs found' and set all_archived=true, masking
a real lychee failure.

Parse the status marker instead of the URL and split the results into
{urls, others}; 'others' are annotated as errors and make all_archived
false with a non-zero exit. Adds a lychee report fixture and regression
tests, and excludes the fixture from lychee's own scan.

Fixes #136

fix(release): defer rate-limited publish and gate downstream artifacts

Treat a crates.io HTTP 429 throttle as a deferred, automatically-recoverable
outcome: publish-crate.rs writes publish_result=rate_limited and exits 0 via a
new FailureKind::is_deferred() predicate, so a transient throttle no longer
turns the release job red. Auth, already-published and unknown failures still
exit non-zero.

GitHub release creation on either an already-published crate or
publish_result == 'success', in both the auto-release and manual-release jobs,
so a deferred upload never produces partial downstream release artifacts. The
same version is retried on the next push to main once the window clears
(check-release-needed.rs keys off crates.io state, not git tags).

function backed by a FailureKind enum (AlreadyExists, AuthFailed,

publish_result=rate_limited outcome with an explanatory banner, instead of
the generic 'failed' / 'Failed to publish for unknown reason'.

The rate-limit banner explains the throttle is transient and that
check-release-needed.rs re-attempts the same version on the next push to
main once the 24-hour window clears (it keys off crates.io publish state,

fix: use per-commit diff instead of full PR diff for change detection

The detect-code-changes script compared GITHUB_BASE_SHA against
GITHUB_HEAD_SHA, which returns all files changed across the entire PR.
This meant a commit touching only .gitkeep would still trigger all CI
jobs because earlier commits in the PR changed code files.

Detect GitHub Actions' synthetic merge commit (where HEAD has two
parents) and use HEAD^2^..HEAD^2 to get the per-commit diff of the
actual PR head. For push events, the regular HEAD^..HEAD is used.
